transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Sara Nguyen (Redwood AE), Amir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CISO - Verdant), Mark Davies (Platform Eng), Priya Shah (Cloud Security), Tom Redd (SRE)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery to validate whether Verdant can use Redwood Hosted or needs Dedicated/Private due to regulatory and data residency constraints. Primary topics: SOC2/ISO certs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption & KMS/HSM, data retention and deletion policies, VPC/on-prem options.

[00:00] Sara: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. I'm Sara from Redwood, and Amir our solutions engineer is with me. Today's goal is to understand Verdant's security needs so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[00:18] Lena: Thanks, Sara. We are evaluating a couple vendors, just want to be clear on where Redwood stands w.r.t SOC2, ISO and the more operational controls.
[00:27] Amir: Totally, and just to say upfront, we have hosted offering that is our fastest onboarding path, dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput and isolation, and a private deployment option for VPC or on-prem with customer-managed networking. We'll walk through controls on each.
[00:40] Mark: The big constraints for us are: we process PHI-ish derived metadata in some flows, our legal wants auditability and key control, and security wants SSO + RBAC integrated.
[00:52] Priya: Also data residency — some datasets need EU-only residency and retention requirements are short, typically 30-90 days for ephemeral logs, but customers data stored for analytics longer; want to see configurable retention.

[02:05] Amir: On compliance: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 — we can share the reports under NDA, and we also publish a security whitepaper and our control matrix. Link: https://redwood.example.com/security (note: placeholder).
[02:21] Lena: Will want to see the latest SOC2 report + bridge letter if applicable. Also curious if you have any FedRAMP or similar?
[02:30] Sara: We don't have FedRAMP yet; primary attestations today are SOC2 Type II and ISO27001, roadmap items include additional certifications for certain enterprise customers. We'll attach the certs after this call.

[04:00] Tom: For SSO, we run Okta + Azure AD. We need SAML 2.0 support and SCIM for provisioning. How does Redwood handle SSO and provisioning?
[04:12] Amir: We support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning in our Console. For Dedicated/Private, SCIM endpoints can be routed via customer-network; for Hosted it works via standard SAML/SCIM endpoints. There are sometimes SCIM attribute mapping quirks — we've got docs and examples.
[04:35] Priya: Any limits on role mapping? We require RBAC at the org, project, and token level — can we restrict token usage to routes or models?
[04:46] Sara: Yes, RBAC exists in the Console — roles like Admin, Developer, Billing, ReadOnly. We also provide token-level permissions for APIs; you can scope keys to models and routes. That's a common ask for production teams.

[06:10] Mark: About audit logs — does Redwood provide immutable audit logs for admin actions, API calls, and model access? We need retention of logs for at least 1 year for internal compliance, and the ability to export to our SIEM.
[06:25] Amir: We capture admin events, user actions in Console, and token-level API access logs. For Hosted, logs are available via our audit logs export and can stream to customer SIEM via secure delivery (S3 or syslog). For Dedicated/Private, logs can be forwarded internally or kept in your VPC; retention policy is configurable. We'll share the log schema.
[06:45] Lena: Is there an append-only thing or tamper-evidence? Our compliance team asks about write-once or signed logs.
[06:54] Amir: We don't currently offer an append-only WORM storage as a built-in product feature, but we support pushing logs to customer-owned S3 buckets with Object Lock enabled, or to your SIEM that provides immutability — that's our recommended pattern. We'll note it as part of the architectural guidance.

[09:05] Priya: Encryption — we need end-to-end encryption at rest and in transit. For customer data, keys must be customer-managed (BYOK) ideally with HSM-backed KMS. How do you support KMS/HSM integrations?
[09:20] Amir: In Hosted we support customer-managed keys through common KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) for encryption at rest of customer artifacts; keys can be rotated. For Dedicated and Private, you can bring-your-own-HSM or connect to your KMS in the VPC. We also encrypt in transit with TLS 1.2/1.3. There are some operational notes around model cache encryption — we can share a tech note.
[10:05] Mark: How about ephemeral KV cache or prefix cache — will customer-provided keys cover cached KV?
[10:13] Amir: Cache encryption depends on deployment: for Hosted caches we manage keys unless you opt into a Dedicated arrangement where we can mount customer-managed encryption. We'll include the caveats in the doc we send.

[12:20] Lena: Data retention and deletion — we need firm guarantees on deletion of PII on request, and proof of deletion for audits. What are your retention windows and deletion semantics?
[12:34] Sara: Default retention on Hosted is 90 days for logs and retained data, but we can configure shorter windows for enterprise customers. For Dedicated/Private you control retention fully. For deletion we have an API to request data deletion and we provide deletion audit evidence; for hosted we provide a certificate of deletion in some cases. There are caveats for backups — they may persist for longer under disaster recovery SLA, but we can provide timelines.
[13:10] Priya: Requesting ability to set per-customer retention policies and per-model retention is critical for us.
[13:18] Amir: That's supported at the org/route level for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we have enterprise customer options that let you set custom retention and log export policies.

[15:00] Tom: Network segmentation — if we go Hosted, we want private networking options and IP allowlisting, plus VPC peering or PrivateLink. What do you support?
[15:12] Sara: For Hosted we provide IP allowlists and PrivateLink on some cloud providers; Dedicated includes private VPC peering; Private deployment is fully in your network. We'll share the network diagram.

[16:30] Mark: Performance/security tradeoffs — if we do full BYOK and our HSM in front of keys, are there latency implications for inference workloads?
[16:45] Amir: Potentially yes for synchronous key usage on every request. Our recommended pattern is envelope encryption with session keys — KMS used to unwrap keys during session establishment, then ephemeral keys used for token-level encryption to reduce per-token latency. We'll provide patterns and benchmark notes.

[19:00] Lena: Incident response & breach notification, how fast do you notify customers and what do you share?
[19:10] Sara: We have incident response SLAs documented; for security incidents affecting customer data we notify within our contractual window (typically 72 hours for significant incidents), share root cause analysis and remediation steps, and coordinate with our customers' security teams. We'll provide the incident response runbook excerpt.

[21:20] Priya: For penetration testing and vulnerability disclosures, do you allow customer pen tests and do you have a bug-bounty program?
[21:30] Amir: We have a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy and run periodic pen tests; customers can request specific tests in Dedicated/Private deployments under constraints and scheduling. We also run a public bug bounty program for certain components.

[23:45] Mark: On the legal side — do you have data processing agreements (DPA) and standard contractual clauses for international transfers?
[23:55] Sara: Yes, we have a DPA and we support SCCs. For EU residency we offer regionally isolated deployments in EU cloud providers. We'll attach the DPA template.

[25:20] Tom: Do you persist prompts or outputs for model training?
[25:27] Amir: We do not use customer prompts or outputs to train our models. That's stated in our policy; for Hosted we can also opt to disable retention for calls used in evaluation. We'll share the explicit policy language.

[27:40] Lena: Are there any gaps we should be aware of? For example, you mentioned no FedRAMP — are there other limitations?
[27:50] Sara: The main limitations are region-specific or certification-specific. Some customers require bespoke controls (e.g., full WORM in product) where we recommend bringing external infra (S3 with Object Lock) as a complement. We'll outline these in a gap document.

[30:00] Amir: For a practical recommendation based on what we heard: if Verdant needs full key control, per-customer retention guarantees, and the highest network isolation, Private (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated is the right path. Hosted can be configured for many enterprise controls but has some managed components that can't be fully customer-controlled today.

[31:15] Mark: That makes sense. Pricing delta is a concern; we need a ballpark for Dedicated vs Hosted to present to procurement.
[31:26] Sara: We'll share ranges; Hosted is usage-based and tends to be lower TCO to start, Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit and predictable throughput. We'll include an example cost/throughput sheet.

[33:40] Tom: Onboarding timeline — how long to go from contract to production for Dedicated vs Private?
[33:50] Amir: Dedicated typical timeline 6-8 weeks (provisioning, networking, security review), Private can vary 8-12+ weeks depending on on-prem constraints. Hosted can be immediate to days for API access plus security review.

[36:00] Priya: We'll want to run a short benchmark — can Redwood run a sample throughput/latency test against our data patterns?
[36:10] Amir: Absolutely — Amir to lead that. We'll need a representative prompt set, expected concurrency, and target latency. We'll propose a 2-week POC with runbook.

[38:30] Sara: Quick recap of action items...
[38:35] Sara: I'll send SOC2 and ISO certs and DPA template. Amir will prepare Dedicated runbook and benchmark plan. Lena will share retention/regulatory constraints. Priya will list KMS and HSM requirements. We'll schedule the SE deep dive.

[39:05] Lena: Sounds good. One last Q — support for tokenization/anonymization at ingestion? We want PII masked before hitting model.
[39:15] Amir: We provide client-side libraries and examples for PII redaction and we also have a pre-processing layer customers can run in their VPC before forwarding to Redwood. We'll send the examples.

[41:00] Mark: About exportability — if we decide to stop using Redwood, how do we get our data and how long to purge?
[41:10] Sara: We provide bulk export APIs and will return data in common formats. Purge timelines depend on backups and DR windows — typical full purge can take up to 30 days across backups, but we'll provide deletion certificates as appropriate.

[43:20] Tom: Thanks all, this was helpful.
[43:25] Lena: Thanks. We'll expect the docs and SOC2 shortly.
[43:30] Sara: Thanks everyone, Amir and I will follow up with the doc package and calendar invite for the deep dive.

[46:00] Meeting end.

References/Shared artifacts:
- Security slide deck (to be attached)
- SOC2 Type II report (link / attachment after NDA)
- ISO27001 certificate (link / attachment)
- Dedicated deployment runbook (will be shared)
- Network diagram & log schema (will be shared)

Recap (plain):
Verdant requires SOC2/ISO evidence, SAML/SCIM SSO, RBAC and token scoping, audit logs export + retention, customer-managed KMS/HSM support, configurable retention and deletion semantics, and options for VPC/Private deployment. Redwood recommended Dedicated or Private for full control; Hosted supports many enterprise controls but with managed components. Next: Redwood to send certs and docs, SE to plan benchmark, Verdant to provide retention and KMS requirements.
